questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay based on the graph below. You should start your essay with a brief description of the graph and comment on China's achievements in urbanization. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
As is vividly shown in the line graph above, the degree of urbanization in China rose steadily and remarkably over nearly four decades. Specifically, the proportion of urban population climbed from a mere 19.39% in 1980 to a striking 60.6% in 2019, tripling within the period, with the growth becoming especially rapid after the year 2000.

Behind this rapid urbanization lie China's tremendous achievements. To begin with, decades of sustained economic growth created vast job opportunities in cities, drawing hundreds of millions of rural residents into urban areas. Moreover, forward-looking government policies and large-scale infrastructure construction accelerated the transfer of population and industries from the countryside to towns. Such progress not only reflects the modernization of the nation but also greatly improves people's living standards and promotes balanced regional development.

In conclusion, the impressive climb of the urbanization curve mirrors the remarkable strides China has made. If this momentum is sustained wisely, the country will surely embrace an even brighter and more prosperous future.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: M: It's my last day at work tomorrow. I'll start my new job in two weeks. My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
transcript.zh: M: 明天是我在这儿工作的最后一天。两周后我就要开始新工作了。人力资源经理想在我离职前和我进行一次面谈。

transcript.text: W: Ah, an exit interview. Are you looking forward to it?
transcript.zh: W: 啊，离职面谈。你期待吗？

transcript.text: M: I'm not sure how I feel about it. I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
transcript.zh: M: 我也说不清自己是什么感觉。我辞职是因为我在那家公司长期以来一直很不开心，但我不确定自己是否应该告诉他们真实的感受。

transcript.text: W: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview. The first is release. Unburdening yourself of frustration, and perhaps even anger to someone who isn't a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully freeing.
transcript.zh: W: 在我看来，在离职面谈时把一股激动的真实想法倾泻出来，可能有两个主要好处。第一个是释放。把自己的挫败感，甚至愤怒，倾诉给一个既不是朋友也不是关系亲密的同事的人，可能会让你感到如释重负。

transcript.text: M: And let me guess. The second is that the criticism will, theoretically, help the organization I'm leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did?
transcript.zh: M: 让我猜猜。第二个好处是，这些批评理论上会帮助我即将离开的组织改进，从而确保未来的员工不太可能遇到我所经历的那些问题？

transcript.text: W: That's right. But the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn't happen. An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't. In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential. And the information is used as dirt against another manager, or can be traded among senior managers.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。但公司改进这一点的问题在于，很多时候它并不会发生。离职面谈本应是私下进行的，但往往并不是。在我所在的公司，从这些面谈中获得的信息通常并不保密。这些信息会被用来攻击另一位经理，或者在高层经理之间互相交换。

transcript.text: M: Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose in the interview. There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry. It is a pretty small industry after all.
transcript.zh: M: 你现在让我重新考虑面谈时要透露些什么了。我的名声和我在这个行业建立人脉的能力，总有可能受到影响。毕竟这个行业相当小。

transcript.text: W: Anything you initially gain from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
transcript.zh: W: 你最初因为直抒己见而获得的即时满足，可能会因为损害未来的职业发展前景而在以后失去。

transcript.text: M: Right. Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites.
transcript.zh: M: 对。也许去那些给雇主评分的网站发泄一下，会更好一些。

transcript.text: W: You could. And don't do the interview at all. Exit interviews are not mandatory.
transcript.zh: W: 你可以这么做。也可以完全不参加面谈。离职面谈不是强制性的。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?

options.text: He will tell the management how he really feels.
He will meet his new manager in two weeks.
He is going to attend a job interview.
He is going to leave his present job.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time.信号：被问者自述 I resigned 的直接陈述 。男士开口第一段就说 It's my last day at work tomorrow. I'll start my new job in two weeks.，到第三…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了 tell them how I really feel 这串原词，但男士说的是 I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel（不确定该不该说），是犹豫，不是『他将会说』。把『不确定要不要』听成『他会』，正中圈套。 借用原文：I'll start my new job in two weeks
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项偷用了 in two weeks 这个时间词，但原文是 I'll start my new job in two weeks（两周后开始新工作），根本没提『见新经理』。听到 two weeks 就选 B，是被数字原词牵着走。 借用原文：an exit interview
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：选项借了原文反复出现的 interview 一词，但原文的 conduct an interview with me before I leave 和 an exit interview 是『离职面谈』，而非 a job interview（求职面试）。同一个 interview，性质完全不同。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I resigned ↔ leave his present job resign 等于 leave the job）

questions.evidenceText: I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time.

questions.stem: What does the woman think about the information gained from an exit interview?

options.text: It can be quite useful to senior managers.
It can improve interviewees' job prospects.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P6）：An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't. In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential.信号：supposed to be 表『本应当』的主张 。女士说 An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't，be supposed to 表示…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 carefully analyzed 在录音里找不到对应说法，女士谈的是保密与被滥用，没有提到『仔细分析』。这是凭空添加的内容。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了 senior managers 这个原词，但原文是 traded among senior managers（在高管间被当把柄交易），是负面滥用，而非 useful to senior managers（对高管有用）这种正面评价。听到 senior managers 就选，正中陷阱。 借用原文：injuring your future career prospects
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：选项 improve interviewees' job prospects（改善求职前景）与原文方向相反：录音第8段说乱说话会 injuring your future career prospects（损害前途），是变坏不是变好。极性被反转了。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（supposed to be private ↔ It should be kept private supposed to be 等于 should be）

questions.evidenceText: An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't. In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential.

questions.stem: Why does the man want to rethink what he will say in the coming exit interview?

options.text: It may leave a negative impression on the interviewer.
It may adversely affect his future career prospects.
It may displease his immediate superiors.
It may do harm to his fellow employees.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.信号：it could affect 表担忧的因果句 。男士说 Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose，紧接 There is always a chance tha…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：选项 negative impression on the interviewer 借了话题里的 interview 氛围，但男士担心的是声誉和人脉、行业里的名声，从没提『给面试官留下负面印象』。这是没有依据的添加。
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：选项盗用了第6段 dirt against another manager 的 manager 语境，但那是女士讲『信息被用来对付别的经理』，并非男士改主意是怕惹自己的顶头上司。把别处的内容嫁接到本题原因上，是张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：选项 harm to his fellow employees 在录音里找不到对应：男士担心的是自己的前途，女士谈的是信息被高管滥用，谁都没说会伤到同事。这是凭空捏造的受害对象。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry ↔ adversely affect his future career prospects 声誉人脉受损概括为前途受损）

questions.evidenceText: There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.

questions.stem: What does the man think he had better do?

options.text: Do some practice for the exit interview.
Network with his close friends to find a better employer.
Pour out his frustrations on a rate-your-employer website.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites.信号：Perhaps it would be better 表打算的建议句 。对话临近结尾，男士说 Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by goi…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：选项 Prepare a comprehensive exit report 借了话题里的 exit 一词，造出『写一份详尽的离职报告』，但录音里男士从没说要写报告。这是凭空添加的方案。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 Do some practice for the exit interview 盗用了 exit interview 这一原词，但全程没有任何人提到『为面谈做练习』；女士最后反而说 don't do the interview at all（干脆别做这面谈）。听到 exit interview 就选，正中原词陷阱。 借用原文：my ability to network in the industry
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 Network with his close friends to find a better employer 借了第7段 network in the industry 的 network 一词，但原文的 network 是『在行业建人脉』且是怕受损，并非『找好友另找雇主』。盗 network 来拼错意，是原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（getting things off my chest ↔ Pour out his frustrations get off chest 等于 pour out frustrations）

transcript.text: M: Today, I'm talking to the renowned botanist, Jane Forster.
transcript.zh: M: 今天，我要采访著名植物学家 Jane Forster。

transcript.text: W: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
transcript.zh: W: Henry，谢谢你邀请我参加你的节目。

transcript.text: M: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary. Can you tell us a little about it?
transcript.zh: M: 最近，Jane，自从你最新的纪录片上映以来，你已经成了相当有名的人。能给我们介绍一下这部纪录片吗？

transcript.text: W: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest in equatorial areas of Southeast Asia.
transcript.zh: W: 这部纪录片记录了我在东南亚赤道地区的热带雨林中，考察当地原生植被的一次探险。

transcript.text: M: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
transcript.zh: M: 你确实有机会去一些非常异国情调的地方旅行。

transcript.text: W: It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream.
transcript.zh: W: 老实说，那一点也不光鲜。我们去的地方只能乘独木舟到达，而且小屋里的生活条件至少可以说是很原始。那里没有电，我们的水源就是附近的一条溪流。

transcript.text: M: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
transcript.zh: M: 你们在那里时的天气状况怎么样？

transcript.text: W: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable. At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing. It was too humid to either work or sleep.
transcript.zh: W: 天气完全不利于我们的工作，因为空气湿度几乎让人无法忍受。中午时分，我们就待在小屋里，什么也不做。天气太潮湿了，既没法工作，也没法睡觉。

transcript.text: M: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
transcript.zh: M: 你们团队在丛林里待了多久？

transcript.text: W: Originally, we planned to be there for a month. But in the end, we stayed for only two weeks.
transcript.zh: W: 我们原本计划在那里待一个月，但最后只待了两个星期。

transcript.text: M: Why did you cut the expedition short?
transcript.zh: M: 你们为什么提前结束了这次探险？

transcript.text: W: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching. And we had to evacuate at very short notice.
transcript.zh: W: 旅程过半时，我们收到消息说一场飓风正在逼近，所以不得不在极短的时间内撤离。

transcript.text: M: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
transcript.zh: M: 听起来真是个引人入胜的故事。

transcript.text: W: It was frightening. The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids. We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
transcript.zh: W: 当时很吓人。最快的撤离路线要经过湍急的河流，我们不得不带着所有设备穿过急流。

transcript.text: M: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful?
transcript.zh: M: 那总的来说，这次旅程算是失败了吗？

transcript.text: W: Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
transcript.zh: W: 当然不是。我们收集了大量有关当地植物的资料。

transcript.text: M: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
transcript.zh: M: 你为什么能忍受如此恶劣的条件？

transcript.text: W: Botany is an obsession for me. Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery. And I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
transcript.zh: W: 植物学对我来说是一种痴迷。我去过的许多地方都有令人惊叹的景色，而且我还能结识来自世界各地的各种各样的人。

transcript.text: M: So where will your next destination be?
transcript.zh: M: 那么，你的下一个目的地会是哪里？

transcript.text: W: I haven't decided yet.
transcript.zh: W: 我还没决定。

transcript.text: M: Then we can leave it for another occasion. Thanks.
transcript.zh: M: 那我们下次再聊。谢谢。

questions.stem: What does the man want Jane Forster to talk about?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary. Can you tell us a little about it?信号：主持人的直接请求句 。信号是主持人发出的请求 Can you tell us a little about it?，其中 it 回指上一句的 your latest documentary——一问一请求，正是他想让她…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：unsuccessful journey 借了对话后段主持人那句 was the journey unsuccessful? 的原词，但那是结尾另一问，并非开场主持人请她谈的话题，听到 unsuccessful/journey 就选属于答非所问。 借用原文：my expedition
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：month-long expedition 借了她回答里 my expedition 与 planned to be there for a month 的原词拼成，但主持人开场请她谈的是纪录片本身，不是"为期一月的远征"这件事，属答非所问。 借用原文：the renowned botanist
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：career as a botanist 借了开场 the renowned botanist 的原词，但主持人没有请她谈"植物学家的职业生涯"，只请她谈纪录片，听到 botanist 就选属答非所问。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（your latest documentary ↔ Her latest documentary. 近乎原词对应）

questions.evidenceText: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary. Can you tell us a little about it?

questions.stem: Why does the woman describe her experience as "far from glamorous"?

options.text: She had to live like a vegetarian.
She was caught in a hurricane.
She had to endure many hardships.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream.信号：原话之后的连串列举 。信号是她说完 far from glamorous 后一口气列举多重恶劣条件：accessible only by canoe、living conditions in the hut were…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：live like a vegetarian（像素食者一样生活）极易与录音里 the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest 的 vegetation 听混，但 vegetation 是"植被"、vegetarian 是"素食者"，原文从未说她被迫吃素，属听音致误的相近词陷阱。 借用原文：a hurricane was approaching
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：caught in a hurricane 借了后文 a hurricane was approaching 的原词，但飓风是导致提前结束（第 7 题）的原因，并非她说 far from glamorous 的缘由，张冠李戴到本题。 借用原文：our water supply was a nearby stream
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：water shortage（缺水）盗用了 our water supply was a nearby stream 里的 water，但原文是说"水源是条小溪"（条件简陋），并非缺水；且只取一样困难，与"many hardships"的总括不符。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the living conditions in the hut were primitive ↔ She had to endure many hardships. 多项困难概括为吃苦）

questions.evidenceText: It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream.

questions.stem: Why did the woman and those who went with her end their trip halfway?

options.text: They had no more food in the canoe.
They could no longer bear the humidity.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching. And we had to evacuate at very short notice.信号：received news that + had to 因果链 。信号是 we received news that a hurricane was approaching 接着 we had to evacuate…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：flood（洪水）在录音里从未出现，它借了后文 river rapids（激流）造成的"和水有关"的联想，但原文撤离原因是飓风不是洪水，属凭联想编造的未提及项。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：no more food in the canoe 借了 accessible only by canoe 的 canoe，但原文从没提食物耗尽，独木舟是"进出方式"而非"断粮地点"，听到 canoe 就选属原词陷阱。 借用原文：the humidity was almost unbearable
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：no longer bear the humidity 借了 the humidity was almost unbearable 的 humidity，但潮湿是描述天气难受（第 6/8 题背景），不是中途撤离的原因——撤离是因飓风，张冠李戴到本题。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a hurricane was approaching ↔ A hurricane was coming. approaching 同义于 coming）

questions.evidenceText: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching. And we had to evacuate at very short notice.

questions.stem: What does the woman think of the journey?
questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P16）：Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.信号：强烈否定 + 反转后的正向定调 。信号是主持人问 was the journey unsuccessful?（负面设问），她以 Absolutely not. 强烈否定反转，再用 gathered a massive…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：memorable（难忘）听上去是正面评价，像能套上整段经历，但她对行程的总评落点是"有收获"，原文并未说"难忘"，属凭褒义氛围误推、原文未提及的态度。
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：unbearable 盗自 the humidity was almost unbearable，那是形容潮湿天气难忍，并非她对整段 journey 的评价；况且她明确否定行程失败，态度是正面，与 unbearable 相反。 借用原文：It was frightening.
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：uneventful（平淡无事）与原文截然相反——她经历了飓风逼近、紧急撤离、激流行船，行程绝非平淡，这是把惊险经历反说成平淡的反向干扰。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（We gathered a massive amount of data ↔ It was fruitful. 采集海量数据等于有收获）

questions.evidenceText: Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.

transcript.text: Scientists often use specialized jargon terms while communicating with laymen. Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice. In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms. They also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics. It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text. Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained.
transcript.zh: 科学家在与非专业人士交流时，常常使用专业术语。他们中的大多数人没有意识到这种做法会产生有害影响。一项新的研究显示，在阅读有关自动驾驶汽车和手术机器人等主题的内容时接触到专业术语的人，后来表示自己对科学的兴趣低于阅读相同主题但未使用专业术语的人。他们还觉得自己对科学的了解更少，也没有足够的资格讨论科学话题。值得注意的是，专业术语是否在文中得到定义并没有造成任何差异。即使这些术语得到了解释，读者仍然感到自己与内容缺乏联系，就像那些阅读了未加解释的专业术语的读者一样。

transcript.text: The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers. Hillary Schulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialized words are a signal. Jargon tells people that the message isn't for them.
transcript.zh: 问题在于，专业术语的存在本身就会向读者传递一种令人气馁的信息。该研究的作者希拉里·舒尔曼认为，专业词汇是一种信号。专业术语会告诉人们，这条信息不是为他们准备的。

transcript.text: There's an even darker side to how people react to jargon. In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science. They found the opposite when a text is easier to read. Then people are more persuaded.
transcript.zh: 人们对专业术语的反应还有更为严重的一面。在另一项研究中，研究人员发现，阅读含有专业术语的科学文章会使人们怀疑科学本身。当文本更容易阅读时，他们发现的结果则恰恰相反。这样一来，人们会更容易被说服。

transcript.text: Thus, it's important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects. This is especially true with issues related to public health, like the safety of new medications and the benefits of vaccines. Schulman concedes that the use of jargon is appropriate with scientific audiences. But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language. They need to eliminate jargon.
transcript.zh: 因此，在谈论复杂的科学主题时，清晰地进行交流非常重要。涉及公共卫生的问题尤其如此，例如新药的安全性和疫苗的益处。舒尔曼承认，在面向科学界人士时使用专业术语是恰当的。但希望与公众交流的科学家需要调整自己的语言。他们需要消除专业术语。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the use of jargon terms by experts?

options.text: It diminishes laymen's interest in science.
It ensures the accuracy of their arguments.
It makes their expressions more explicit.
It hurts laymen's dignity and self-esteem.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice. In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms.信号：定性词harmful＋对比 。答案句的信号是定性词 the harmful effects（有害影响）和紧随其后的对比结果 less interested in science：录音先给出"有害"的定性，再用接触术语…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 盗用了术语话题里反复出现的 science 一词，编出 ensures the accuracy of their arguments.（确保论点准确）。但原文只说术语"有害"、让人兴趣下降，从未说它"确保准确"，方向正相反，是听到 science 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：the harmful effects of this practice
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 说术语 makes their expressions more explicit.（使表达更清晰），是正面作用；但原文定性是 the harmful effects，且第 2 段说术语 sends a discouraging message，方向与 C 完全相反，属与原文相反的干扰。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 说术语 hurts laymen's dignity and self-esteem.（伤害外行尊严与自尊）。原文确实讲了多种负面后果——兴趣下降、感觉 less informed、less qualified to discuss，但从未提"尊严/自尊"，dignity、self-esteem 是原文没出现的概念，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（less interested in science ↔ diminishes laymen's interest in science 形容词改写为动词）

questions.stem: What does Schulman suggest scientists do when communicating with the general public?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language. They need to eliminate jargon.信号：转折But＋建议need to 。双重信号：先是转折 But（前句说术语对专业听众尚可，But 后才是对大众的真正主张），再是建议动词 need to eliminate jargon。转折后＋need to 之处，…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 说要 Find appropriate topics.（找合适话题）。原文给的建议是"去掉术语"，全篇没谈"挑选话题"，topics 虽在前文出现过（如 read about the same topics），但从未作为给科学家的建议，属未提及。

transcript.text: At the beginning of the twentieth century, on the Gulf Coast in the US state of Texas, there was a hill where gas leakage was so noticeable that schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire.
transcript.zh: 二十世纪初，在美国得克萨斯州的墨西哥湾沿岸，有一座山丘，那里天然气泄漏十分明显，以至于学生们有时会把山丘点燃。

transcript.text: Pattillo Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill. Oil wells weren't drilled back then; they were essentially dug. The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole. Higgins had forecast oil at 1,000 feet, a totally made-up figure.
transcript.zh: 帕蒂洛·希金斯是一名声名狼藉的当地商人，他确信这座冒气的山丘下方有石油。那时还没有钻探油井；油井基本上是挖出来的。山丘下的沙土使希金斯的工人几次试图挖出合适井孔的努力都以失败告终。希金斯预言一千英尺深处会有石油，这个数字完全是凭空捏造的。

transcript.text: Higgins subsequently hired a mining engineer, Captain Anthony Lucas. After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry.
transcript.zh: 随后，希金斯聘请了一名采矿工程师安东尼·卢卡斯上尉。在经历了几次挫折后，卢卡斯上尉决定使用钻机，他的创新创造了现代石油钻探业。

transcript.text: In January 1901, at 1,020 feet-almost precisely the depth predicted by Higgins' wild guess—the well roared and suddenly ejected mud and six tons of drilling pipe out of the ground, terrifying those present. For the next nine days, until the well was capped, the well poured out more oil than all the wells in America combined.
transcript.zh: 1901年1月，在一千零二十英尺深处——几乎正是希金斯那个荒唐猜测所预言的深度——油井发出轰鸣，突然将泥浆和六吨钻管从地下喷出，把在场的人吓坏了。在接下来的九天里，直到油井被封住为止，它涌出的石油超过了美国所有油井产量的总和。

transcript.text: In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry; cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy. Higgins' well changed that. The boom made some prospectors millionaires, but the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas. In the 1930s, prices crashed, to the point that in some parts of the country oil was cheaper than water. That would become a familiar pattern of the boom-or-bust Texas' economy.
transcript.zh: 那时，得克萨斯州几乎完全是农村地区，没有大城市，实际上也没有工业；棉花和牛肉是经济的基础。希金斯的油井改变了这一切。这场繁荣使一些勘探者成为百万富翁，但石油突然过剩对得克萨斯州而言并不完全是福音。到了20世纪30年代，油价暴跌，在美国一些地区，石油甚至比水还便宜。这后来成为得克萨斯州经济繁荣或萧条的一个常见模式。

transcript.text: Most people dislike their jobs. It's an astonishing but statistical fact. A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers. Few describe their managers as malicious or manipulative though. While those types certainly exist, they are a minority. The majority of managers, seemingly, just don't know any better. They are often emulating bad managers they've had in the past. It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course. They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style.
transcript.zh: 大多数人不喜欢自己的工作。这是一个令人惊讶却有统计数据支持的事实。根据最新研究，员工不满的一个主要原因是，许多人认为自己的经理非常糟糕。不过，很少有人把自己的经理描述为恶意或善于操纵他人的人。虽然这类人确实存在，但他们只是少数。显然，大多数经理只是缺乏更好的管理方法。他们往往是在模仿自己过去遇到过的糟糕经理。他们很可能从未读过管理类书籍，也没有参加过管理课程。他们甚至可能从未认真思考过良好的管理应该是什么样，以及良好的管理会如何影响自己的管理风格。

transcript.text: The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had. From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs.
transcript.zh: 研究人员就经理的表现采访了员工，首先询问他们曾经遇到过的最糟糕的经理。根据这些访谈，研究人员归纳出一些经理被认为工作能力极差的四个主要原因。

transcript.text: The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices. It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy. Often a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings. Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.
transcript.zh: 第一个原因是企业文化，员工认为企业文化助长了糟糕的管理方式。研究发现，最应受指责的具体因素是压力很大的工作环境、极少的培训以及缺乏问责。经理的上级在未能惩处经理的不当行为时，往往实际上是在助长这种令人反感的行为。这类工作场所有时被称为有毒的工作环境。

transcript.text: The second cause was attributed to the managers' characteristics. Those deemed to be most destructive were odd people—those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace, and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general.
transcript.zh: 第二个原因归结于经理自身的特点。被认为最具破坏性的是一些古怪的人——缺乏进取心的人、把个人问题带入工作场所的人，以及总体上脾气或性格令人不快的人。

transcript.text: The third cause of poor management was associated with a deficiency of qualifications not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university, but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments.
transcript.zh: 管理不善的第三个原因与资历不足有关，这里的资历并不主要指从大学获得的正式学历，而是指通过可信的工作经历和职业成就积累起来的非正式资历。

transcript.text: The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential. One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest. It wasn't their skill set or other merits that got them the job; it was their tenure.
transcript.zh: 第四个原因涉及那些因潜力以外的理由而获得晋升的经理。其中一个特别的原因是，他们在公司待的时间最长。让他们得到这份工作的并不是他们的技能或其他优点，而是他们的任职年限。

transcript.text: A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees. The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers. It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing, merrily ignorant of the damage they're actually causing, which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager.
transcript.zh: 值得指出的是，这项研究仅基于员工的视角。研究人员没有询问高层领导如何看待他们的一线经理。他们很可能对自己提拔的人如今的表现感到满意，却完全没有意识到这些人实际上造成的损害；这或许可以解释为什么研究人员得出结论认为，那些同样的中层经理通常并不知道自己是一名糟糕的经理。

questions.stem: What is a primary cause of employee dissatisfaction according to recent research?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers.信号：题干原话几乎照搬的点题句 。录音开篇第二句就用 A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that…，与…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：Unsuitable jobs.（不合适的岗位）录音通篇未提，整段都在讲管理者的问题，从没说员工不满是因为岗位不对口，属凭常识自行脑补的归因。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：Insufficient motivation.（动力不足）看似呼应录音后文谈管理者「缺乏 drive（干劲）」的描述，但那是在说坏管理者的个人特征（第 4 段），不是员工不满的主因；它把「动力」这个似曾相识的概念安到了错误的问题上。
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：Tough regulations.（严苛的规章）勉强能让人联想到第 3 段的 toxic 工作环境，但录音从未把「规章严苛」列为员工不满的主因；本题问的是开篇点明的 primary cause，规章既非原话、也非主因。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（they have terrible managers ↔ Bad managers. terrible 同义改写为 bad）

questions.evidenceText: A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers.

questions.stem: What is one of the causes for poor management practices?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices. It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy. Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.信号：分点信号 The first cause + 收尾点出 toxic 。录音用 The first cause was company culture 起头明确这是分点罗列的第一条成因，又在段末用 Such workp…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Ineffective training.（无效的培训）盗用了录音 minimal training（极少的培训）里的 training 一词来勾人，但录音说的是培训「太少」，不是培训「无效」；况且 minimal training 只是 company culture 这条大成因下的一个细节，本身不是独立成因。 借用原文：a lack of accountability
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：Lack of regular evaluation.（缺少定期评估）借用了录音 a lack of accountability（缺乏问责）的 lack of 句式来制造耳熟感，但 accountability（问责）≠ evaluation（评估），录音从未说缺少「定期评估」；这是把一个近形概念偷换进来。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：Overburdening of managers.（管理者负担过重）听起来像在替管理者开脱，但录音四条成因（公司文化、管理者性格、资历不足、靠资历晋升）里没有一条说管理者「负担过重」，纯属未提及。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The first cause was company culture ↔ Toxic company culture. company culture 原词 + toxic 由原文回收）

questions.evidenceText: The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices. It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy. Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the study on job dissatisfaction?

options.text: It collected feedback from both employers and employees.
It was conducted from frontline managers' point of view.
It provided meaningful clues to solving the problem.
It was based only on the perspective of employees.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees. The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers.信号：结尾提示语 A point worth making + only 。录音末段用 A point worth making is that…（有一点值得说明）这种「特意提醒」的强调语引出关键句，后面紧跟 the st…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：It collected feedback from both employers and employees.（向雇主和雇员双方收集反馈）盗用了录音里真实出现的 employees 一词，却把范围从「只问员工」夸成「双方都问」；录音明说 The researchers didn't ask senior leaders，恰恰否定了 both。 借用原文：what they thought of their frontline managers
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：It was conducted from frontline managers' point of view.（研究从一线管理者的视角进行）搬来了录音 their frontline managers 这个原词，但录音说研究是从员工视角做的，frontline managers 是被评价的对象、不是研究的视角；选项把视角张冠李戴了。
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：It provided meaningful clues to solving the problem.（研究为解决问题提供了有价值的线索）是一句听起来很顺、很积极的评价，但末段只交代研究的取材局限（只问员工、高层没问），从没说它给出了「解决问题的有价值线索」，属凭常识脑补的拔高。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the study was based only on the perspective of employees ↔ It was based only on the perspective of employees. 几乎逐词对应的复述）

questions.evidenceText: A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees. The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers.

transcript.text: With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.
transcript.zh: 随着无人驾驶车辆的使用似乎已不可避免，位于澳大利亚广袤沙漠州西澳大利亚州的矿业公司无疑走在了前列。

transcript.text: Iron ore is a key ingredient in steel-making. The mining companies here produce almost 300 million tons of iron ore a year. The 240 giant autonomous trucks in use, in the Western Australian mines, can weigh 400 tons, fully loaded, and travel at speeds of up to 60 kilometers per hour. They are a technological leap, transporting iron ore along routes which run for hundreds of kilometers from mines to their destinations. Here when the truck arrives at its destination, staff in the operation center direct it precisely where to unload. Vast quantities of iron ore are then transported by autonomous trains to ocean ports.
transcript.zh: 铁矿石是炼钢的关键原料。这里的矿业公司每年生产近3亿吨铁矿石。西澳大利亚州矿区正在使用的240辆巨型自动驾驶卡车满载时重量可达400吨，行驶速度最高可达每小时60公里。它们是技术上的一大飞跃，沿着数百公里长的路线，将铁矿石从矿山运往目的地。当卡车抵达目的地时，运营中心的工作人员会精确指挥它在指定位置卸货。随后，大量铁矿石由自动驾驶列车运往海港。

transcript.text: Advocates argue these automated vehicles will change mining forever. It may only be five years before the use of automation technology leads to a fully robotic mine.
transcript.zh: 支持者认为，这些自动化车辆将永远改变采矿业。自动化技术的应用可能只需五年就会促成一座完全由机器人运作的矿山。

transcript.text: A range of factors has pushed Western Australia's desert region to the lead of this automation revolution. These include the huge size of the mines, the scale of equipment and the repetitive nature of some of the work. Then there's the area's remoteness. At 502,000 square kilometers, it can sometimes make recruiting staff a challenge. Another consideration is the risks when humans interact with large machinery. There are also the financial imperatives. The ongoing push by the mining corporations to be more productive and more efficient is another powerful driver in embracing automation technology.
transcript.zh: 多种因素推动西澳大利亚的沙漠地区走在这场自动化革命的前沿。这些因素包括矿山规模庞大、设备规模巨大，以及部分工作具有重复性。此外，还有该地区地处偏远这一因素。这里面积达50.2万平方公里，有时会使招聘员工成为一项挑战。另一个需要考虑的因素是人类与大型机械互动时所面临的风险。此外还有财务方面的迫切需求。矿业公司持续推动提高生产率和效率，也是其积极采用自动化技术的另一个强大动力。

transcript.text: The concept of a fully autonomous mine is a bit of a misleading term, however. This is because the more technology is put into the field, the more people are needed to deploy, maintain and improve it.
transcript.zh: 不过，将完全自动化的矿山称为“完全自主矿山”有些误导。因为投入现场的技术越多，就越需要更多人员来部署、维护和改进这些技术。

transcript.text: The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for different jobs. These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence. The mining companies claim automation and robotics present opportunities to make mining more sustainable and safer. Employees will be offered a career that is even more fulfilling and more rewarding.
transcript.zh: 行业的自动化和数字化正在催生对不同岗位的需求，其中包括数据科学家以及从事自动化和人工智能工作的工程师。矿业公司声称，自动化和机器人技术为实现更加可持续、更安全的采矿创造了机会。员工将获得一份更加充实、回报也更加丰厚的职业。

transcript.text: Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology. But they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology. Their main concern is the potential impact on remote communities. As automation spreads further, the question is how these remote communities will survive when the old jobs are eliminated. And this may well prove to be the most significant impact of robotic technology in many places around the world.
transcript.zh: 工人协会已经接受新技术引入的必然性。但它们仍然对自动化技术的发展持保留态度。它们最主要的担忧是自动化可能对偏远社区造成的影响。随着自动化进一步普及，问题在于，当原有工作岗位被取消后，这些偏远社区将如何生存。而这很可能会成为机器人技术在世界许多地方产生的最重大的影响。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the mining industry in Western Australia?

options.text: It is seeing an automation revolution.
It is bringing prosperity to the region.
It is yielding an unprecedented profit.
It is expanding at an accelerating speed.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.信号：开头点题的总括句 。篇章独白的总判断常落在开头：录音第一句 mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are …

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 bringing prosperity to the region 借用了录音里反复出现的地域词（desert state、remote communities）制造熟悉感，但录音第一句讲的是该矿业领先于自动化，并未说它给地区带来繁荣，属听到地域词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：They are a technological leap
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 yielding an unprecedented profit 听上去与矿业赚钱顺理成章，但录音开头讲的是技术领先，全文只提到 financial imperatives、more productive 这类追求效率的动因，从未说产出空前利润，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项 expanding at an accelerating speed 蹭了录音里 taking the lead、a technological leap 的进取气势，但录音说的是矿业在自动化技术上领先、是技术跃进，而非整个行业在加速扩张规模，把技术领先偷换成了规模扩张。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（driverless vehicles ↔ automation 无人驾驶=自动化的同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.

questions.stem: What is the impact of the digitization of the mining industry?

options.text: It creates a lot of new jobs.
It causes conflicts between employers and employees.
It calls for the retraining of unskilled mining workers.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for different jobs. These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence.信号：因果动词 creating 引出影响 。录音第 6 段 The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for differen…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：选项 exhausts resources sooner 借矿业必然涉及资源的常识制造合理感，但录音通篇讲数字化带来岗位变化与可持续，从未说它更快耗尽资源，原文无此判断。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 conflicts between employers and employees 蹭了录音里 employees、workers' unions 这些词，但录音讲工会有保留是出于对偏远社区的担忧，并未说数字化在劳资双方间引发冲突，把工会的保留偷换成了劳资对立。 借用原文：data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项 retraining of unskilled mining workers 借用了录音里的 mining、workers，但录音说数字化需要的是数据科学家、工程师这类新型人才，并未提对非技术矿工的再培训，把催生新岗位偷换成了再培训旧工人。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（creating a need for different jobs ↔ creates a lot of new jobs 催生岗位需求=创造新岗位）

questions.evidenceText: The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for different jobs. These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence.

questions.stem: What is the attitude of workers' unions towards the introduction of new technology?

options.text: They welcome it with open arms.
They will wait to see its effect.
They are strongly opposed to it.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P7）：Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology. But they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology.信号：转折 But 后才是真态度 。录音先说工会 accepted（接受），紧接 But they still have reservations 用 But 转出真态度——仍有保留。态度题的落点在转折之后，前半的接受只是…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：选项 welcome it with open arms 把工会的态度拔高成热烈欢迎，只接住了 But 前的 accepted，丢了 But 后的 reservations，态度偏正、过头了。 借用原文：the most significant impact of robotic technology
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 wait to see its effect 借用了录音里讲影响（impact、effect）的语境制造熟悉感，但录音说工会已经接受、只是有保留，并非按兵不动地观望效果，原文无观望此意。 借用原文：they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：选项 strongly opposed to it 抓住录音里 reservations、main concern 的负面情绪，把有保留放大成强烈反对，但工会明说已经 accepted，并未反对，态度极性反了。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（have accepted the inevitability ↔ accept it 接受=accept，态度同向）

questions.evidenceText: Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology. But they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology.

transcript.text: According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road-death rate is almost double the global average. Thai people know that their roads are dangerous, but they don't know this could easily be changed.
transcript.zh: 根据官方统计，泰国每年的道路死亡率几乎是全球平均水平的两倍。泰国人知道本国道路十分危险，但他们不知道这种状况其实很容易改变。

transcript.text: Globally, road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease. Researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in America put the death toll in 2017 at 1.24 million. According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century. But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.
transcript.zh: 在全球范围内，道路事故每年造成的死亡人数超过任何一种传染病。美国健康指标与评估研究所的研究人员估计，2017年的死亡人数为124万。据该研究所称，自本世纪初以来，死亡总人数基本保持不变。但这一数字掩盖了各个国家发生的诸多变化。

transcript.text: In many poor countries, road accidents are killing more people than ever before. Those countries have swelling, young populations, a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes, and a limited supply of surgeons. It is impossible to know for sure because official statistics are so inadequate, but deaths are thought to have risen by 40% since 1990 in many low-income countries. In many rich countries, by contrast, roads are becoming even safer. In Estonia and Ireland, for example, the number of deaths has fallen by about two-thirds since the late 1990s.
transcript.zh: 在许多贫穷国家，道路事故造成的死亡人数比以往任何时候都多。这些国家人口不断增长且较为年轻，汽车和摩托车数量快速增加，而外科医生数量有限。由于官方统计数据严重不足，无法确切得知实际情况，但据认为，许多低收入国家的死亡人数自1990年以来增加了40%。相比之下，在许多富裕国家，道路正变得更加安全。例如，在爱沙尼亚和爱尔兰，死亡人数自20世纪90年代末以来减少了约三分之二。

transcript.text: But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle-income countries, which contain most of the world's people and have some of the most dangerous roads. According to researchers, in China and South Africa, traffic deaths have been falling since 2000, and in India since 2012, and the Philippines reached its peak four years ago. The question is whether Thailand can soon follow suit.
transcript.zh: 但最重要、也最引人关注的变化发生在中等收入国家。这些国家拥有世界上大多数人口，也有一些最危险的道路。据研究人员称，在中国和南非，交通事故死亡人数自2000年以来一直在下降；在印度，这一趋势始于2012年；菲律宾则在四年前达到峰值。问题在于，泰国能否很快步其后尘。

transcript.text: Rob MeInerney, head of the International Road Assessment Programme, says that all countries tend to go through three phases. They begin with poor, slow roads. In the second phase, as they grow wealthier, they pave the roads, allowing traffic to move faster and pushing up the death rate. Lastly, in the third phase, countries act to make their roads safer. The trick, then, is to reach the third stage sooner, by focusing earlier and more closely on fatal accidents.
transcript.zh: International Road Assessment Programme负责人Rob MeInerney表示，所有国家往往都会经历三个阶段。第一阶段是道路状况差、通行速度慢。第二阶段，随着国家变得更加富裕，道路得到铺设，车辆行驶速度加快，死亡率也随之上升。最后，在第三阶段，各国采取措施提高道路安全性。因此，关键在于更早、更集中地关注致命事故，从而尽快进入第三阶段。

transcript.text: How to do that? The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives. Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow but often don't. Dangerous driving is not a fixed cultural trait, as some imagine. People respond to incentives, such as traffic laws that are actually enforced.
transcript.zh: 如何做到这一点？解决办法不仅在于改善基础设施，也在于建立更好的社会激励机制。安全驾驶习惯是人们知道自己应该遵守、却常常不去遵守的行为规范。危险驾驶并不是某些人所认为的那种固定的文化特征。人们会对激励措施作出反应，例如真正得到执行的交通法规。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about traffic accidents in Thailand?

options.text: Their cost to the nation's economy is incalculable.
They kill more people than any infectious disease.
Their annual death rate is about twice that of the global average.
They have experienced a gradual decline since the year of 2017.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road-death rate is almost double the global average.信号：地名加数字即落点 。第一段开门见山点出 Thailand's annual road-death rate is almost double the global average，地名 Thailand 加上倍数 d…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：Their cost to the nation's economy is incalculable. 谈经济成本不可估量，录音第一段只说死亡率高、并说这本可改变，从未提及对经济的成本，属凭常识脑补的无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：They kill more people than any infectious disease. 里的 infectious disease 确实在录音出现，但那是第二段讲全球情况 road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease，主语是 Globally 而非泰国，被错安到了泰国头上。 借用原文：the death toll in 2017
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：They have experienced a gradual decline since the year of 2017 说泰国死亡率自 2017 年逐渐下降，2017 这个年份录音第二段 the death toll in 2017 确实念到，但那是全球死亡人数的统计年份，且原文说泰国道路危险本可改变、并无下降之说，极性正好相反。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（almost double the global average ↔ about twice that of the global average double 同义于 twice）

questions.stem: What do we learn from an American institute's statistics regarding road deaths?

options.text: They show a difference between rich and poor nations.
They don't reflect the changes in individual countries.
They rise and fall from year to year.
They are not as reliable as claimed.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century. But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.信号：转折 But 后才是真意 。前半句说总数基本平稳，紧接 But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries，转折词 But 之后才是说话人真正强调的…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：They show a difference between rich and poor nations. 说贫富差异——贫富国家的对比确在录音第三段出现 In many poor countries … In many rich countries, by contrast，但那是后文展开的内容，并非这组美国机构统计本身得出的结论，题干问的恰是这组统计，张冠李戴了。 借用原文：has been more or less static since the turn of the century

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A hundred years before iconic figures like Bill Gates and Steve Jobs permeated our lives, an Irish-Italian inventor laid the foundation of the communication explosion of the 21st century. Guglielmo Marconi was arguably the first truly global figure in modern communication. Not only was he the first to communicate globally, he was the first to think globally about communication. Marconi may not have been the greatest inventor of his time, but more than anyone else, he brought about a fundamental shift in the way we communicate.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Today's globally networked media and communication system has its origins in the 19th century, when, for the first time, messages were sent electronically across great distances. The telegraph, the telephone, and radio were the obvious predecessors of the Internet, iPods, and mobile phones. What made the link from then to now was the development of wireless communication. Marconi was the first to develop and perfect this system, using the recently-discovered "air waves" that make up the electromagnetic spectrum.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Between 1896, when he applied for his first patent in England at the age of 22, and his death in Italy in 1937, Marconi was at the center of every major innovation in electronic communication. He was also a skilled and sophisticated organizer, an entrepreneurial innovator, who mastered the use of corporate strategy, media relations, government lobbying, international diplomacy, patents, and prosecution. Marconi was really interested in only one thing: the extension of mobile, personal, long-distance communication to the ends of the earth (and beyond, if we can believe some reports). Some like to refer to him as a genius, but if there was any genius to Marconi it was this vision.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: In 1901 he succeeded in signaling across the Atlantic, from the west coast of England to Newfoundland in the USA, despite the claims of science that it could not be done. In 1924 he convinced the British government to encircle the world with a chain of wireless stations using the latest technology that he had devised, shortwave radio. There are some who say Marconi lost his edge when commercial broadcasting came along; he didn't see that radio could or should be used to frivolous(无聊的) ends. In one of his last public speeches, a radio broadcast to the United States in March 1937, he deplored that broadcasting had become a one-way means of communication and foresaw it moving in another direction, toward communication as a means of exchange. That was visionary genius.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Marconi's career was devoted to making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly, and with an elegance that would appear to be intuitive and uncomplicated to the user-friendly, if you will. There is a direct connection from Marconi to today's social media, search engines, and program streaming that can best be summed up by an admittedly provocative exclamation: the 20th century did not exist. In a sense, Marconi's vision jumped from his time to our own.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Marconi invented the idea of global communication—or, more straightforwardly, globally networked, mobile, wireless communication. Initially, this was wireless Morse code telegraphy(电报通讯), the principal communication technology of his day. Marconi was the first to develop a practical method for wireless telegraphy using radio waves. He borrowed technical details from many sources, but what set him apart was a self-confident vision of the power of communication technology on the one hand, and, on the other, of the steps that needed to be taken to consolidate his own position as a player in that field. Tracing Marconi's lifeline leads us into the story of modern communication itself. There were other important figures, but Marconi towered over them all in reach, power, and influence, as well as in the grip he had on the popular imagination of his time. Marconi was quite simply the central figure in the emergence of a modern understanding of communication.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In his lifetime, Marconi foresaw the development of television and the fax machine, GPS, radar, and the portable hand-held telephone. Two months before he died, newspapers were reporting that he was working on a "death ray," and that he had "killed a rat with an intricate device at a distance of three feet." By then, anything Marconi said or did was newsworthy. Stock prices rose or sank according to his pronouncements. If Marconi said he thought it might rain, there was likely to be a run on umbrellas.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Marconi's biography is also a story about choices and the motivations behind them. At one level, Marconi could be fiercely autonomous and independent of the constraints of his own social class. On another scale, he was a perpetual outsider. Wherever he went, he was never "of" the group; he was always the "other," considered foreign in Britain, British in Italy, and "not American" in the United States. At the same time, he also suffered tremendously from a need for acceptance that drove, and sometimes stained, every one of his relationships.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Marconi placed a permanent stamp on the way we live. He was the first person to imagine a practical application for the wireless spectrum, and to develop it successfully into a global communication system—in both terms of the word; that is, worldwide and all-inclusive. He was able to do this because of a combination of factors—most important, timing and opportunity—but the single-mindedness and determination with which he carried out his self-imposed mission was fundamentally character-based; millions of Marconi's contemporaries had the same class, gender, race, and colonial privilege as he, but only a handful did anything with it. Marconi needed to achieve the goal that was set in his mind as an adolescent; by the time he reached adulthood, he understood, intuitively, that in order to have an impact he had to both develop an independent economic base and align himself with political power. Disciplined, uncritical loyalty to political power became his compass for the choices he had to make.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: At the same time, Marconi was uncompromisingly independent intellectually. Shortly after Marconi's death, the nuclear physicist Enrico Fermi—soon to be the developer of the Manhattan Project—wrote that Marconi proved that theory and experimentation were complementary features of progress. "Experience can rarely, unless guided by a theoretical concept, arrive at results of any great significance…on the other hand, an excessive trust in theoretical conviction would have prevented Marconi from persisting in experiments which were destined to bring about a revolution in the technique of radio-communications." In other words, Marconi had the advantage of not being burdened by preconceived assumptions.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: The most controversial aspect of Marconi's life—and the reason why there has been no satisfying biography of Marconi until now—was his uncritical embrace of Benito Mussolini. At first this was not problematic for him. But as the regressive(倒退的) nature of Mussolini's regime became clear, he began to suffer a crisis of conscience. However, after a lifetime of moving within the circles of power, he was unable to break with authority, and served Mussolini faithfully (as president of Italy's national research council and royal academy, as well as a member of the Fascist Grand Council) until the day he died—conveniently—in 1937, shortly before he would have had to take a stand in the conflict that consumed a world that he had, in part, created.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Humans are fascinated by the source of their failings and virtues: This preoccupation inevitably leads to an old debate: whether nature or nurture moulds us more. A revolution in genetics has poised this as a modern political question about the character of our society: if personalities are hard-wired into our genes, what can governments do to help us? It feels morally questionable, yet claims of genetic selection by intelligence are making headlines.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: This is down to "hereditarian"(遗传论的) science and a recent paper claimed "differences in exam performance between pupils attending selective and non-selective schools mirror the genetic differences between them". With such an assertion, the work was predictably greeted by a lot of absurd claims about "genetics determining academic success". What the research revealed was the rather less surprising result: the educational benefits of selective schools largely disappear once pupils' inborn ability and socio-economic background were taken into account. It is a glimpse of the blindingly obvious—and there's nothing to back strongly either a hereditary or environmental argument.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Yet the paper does say children are "unintentionally genetically selected" by the school system. Central to hereditarian science is a tall claim: that identifiable variations in genetic sequences can predict an individual's aptness to learn, reason and solve problems. This is problematic on many levels. A teacher could not seriously tell a parent their child has a low genetic tendency to study when external factors clearly exist. Unlike-minded academics say the inheritability of human traits is scientifically unsound. At best there is a weak statistical association and not a causal link between DNA and intelligence. Yet sophisticated statistics are used to create an intimidatory atmosphere of scientific certainty.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: While there's an undoubted genetic basis to individual difference, it is wrong to think that socially defined groups can be genetically accounted for. The fixation on genes as destiny is surely false too. Medical predictability can rarely be based on DNA alone; the environment matters too. Something as complex as intellect is likely to be affected by many factors beyond genes. If hereditarians want to advance their cause it will require more balanced interpretation and not just acts of advocacy.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Genetic selection is a way of exerting influence over others, "the ultimate collective control of human destinies," as writer H. G. Wells put it. Knowledge becomes power and power requires a sense of responsibility. In understanding cognitive ability, we must not elevate discrimination to a science, allowing people to climb the ladder of life only as far as their cells might suggest. This will need a more sceptical eye on the science. As technology progresses, we all have a duty to make sure that we shape a future that we would want to find ourselves in.
